world: Linear systems x' = A x with candidate sensors: a diffusion chain with Dirichlet ends (stable), the Lorenz-96 Jacobian at its fixed point x_i = F (unstable, the growth world), a linearised one-dimensional shallow-water grid (neutral), and, on the run only, a periodic advection-diffusion chain (unseen family). Candidate sensors on chains and Lorenz-96 read a seeded weighted average of two adjacent coordinates; on the shallow-water grid they read h or u at one cell. The read operator of a placement is the exact window Gramian over [0, T]. The window is T = 0.5. Thresholds c = frac x lambda_max of the all-sensor Gramian, frac in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}, set the budget B = sqrt(c) rho; required counts m in {4, 6, 8, 10}. Beside the greedy count each cell records the count the energy ranking needs to reach m and the median count a random ordering needs, so the cells where placement matters are visible. The pilot worlds are smaller (n = 16, 16, 20) with their own sensor draw; the run worlds are the declared sizes with fresh draws.
